sequencer.intro: A desk instrument built from one CV. Pick a mode at the bottom, press pads, turn knobs. The printed manual below the device holds every entry in plain text.
sequencer.honesty: the device is an illustration. Years, roles, projects and skills come from the CV; the algorithm inputs are short synthetic sequences.

how.kmer: A window of length k slides along the sequence one base at a time; every window is one k-mer. Counting them gives a k-mer spectrum, used for genome-size estimates, error correction and alignment-free comparison. Turn the knob to change k and step the window with the transport keys.
how.seed: Seed-and-extend search tools first look for short exact matches. A spaced seed only compares the positions marked 1 and ignores the 0s, so a hit survives mismatches at the ignored positions — it finds more distant similarities with the same seed weight (PatternHunter, 2002). Toggle mask positions with pads 5–12 and move the target offset with the knob.
how.nw: Needleman–Wunsch fills an (n+1)×(m+1) matrix: each cell takes the best of a diagonal step (match or mismatch score), a step down or a step right (gap penalty). The bottom-right cell is the optimal global alignment score; following the pointers back gives the alignment. Step through the fill, change the scores with the knobs and watch the traceback.

f1.title: Skill domains, linked by the projects that use them
f1.caption: Outer ideogram: {domains, number} skill domains and the soft skills; arc length is proportional to the number of skills, one tick per skill ({skills, number} in total). Numbers under each label: skills · projects. Coloured track: projects per domain. Ribbons: the {chords, number} domain pairs that share projects; a ribbon's width is the number of projects (of {projects, number}) whose tags match skills in both domains. Select a domain below to isolate its ribbons; select a ribbon for the projects behind it.

f2.title: pRY2026 — a plasmid map of the career
f2.caption: The backbone is the timeline from {lo} to {hi}, read clockwise from ori at the top (kept clockwise in every language, as plasmid maps are). The {count, number} arrows are the dated degrees and roles, coloured by kind; overlapping periods stack outwards on separate lanes. The gold MCS (multiple cloning site) marks the Saarbrücken period, where new parts are being inserted — a metaphor. {undated, plural, =0 {} one {The # role without dates is listed in table S2.} other {The # roles without dates are listed in table S2.}}

f3.title: Growth rings: one ring per year
f3.caption: Rings run from {lo} (centre) to {hi} (bark). Ring shade is proportional to course hours that year; right half: one tick per course; bottom: red dots for publications with a year; left half: one dot per role or degree active that year, coloured by kind. Select a ring or a year for the entries.

f4.title: From project categories to skill domains
f4.caption: Sankey diagram: project categories (left) flow into skill domains (right). A link's width is the number of projects of that category whose tags match the domain. A project that matches several domains contributes to each, so bar heights count project–domain matches, while the numbers next to the labels count projects. Domains without a matching project are left out.
